explainer.title: Why do some positions move while we hold the #1 share of organic traffic?
body: Share of organic traffic is a presence score: across the charities we track, it measures how much of the combined organic search traffic RMBH captures compared with everyone else. Right now, among the direct Rabbi Meir Baal Haness charities, RMBH draws 48.25% of that traffic and ranks #1 of 4, 1.8x the next organization (Kupath Rabbi Meir at 26.72%). That standing holds even while a handful of individual keyword positions tick up or down, because the overall traffic share is the whole picture while a single keyword's rank is one pixel inside it. A few terms slipping a spot or two barely moves the overall total. It is the difference between a team's season record and the score of one quarter.

There are three real reasons individual positions move, and none of them mean we are losing ground. First, demand is seasonal: people search for giving and prayer terms in waves, and Google reshuffles results to match. In Semrush's own data, searches for "donate to charity" swing more than 4x between their quietest and busiest month, and "jewish charity" swings over 6x, so the same page naturally rises and falls with the calendar even when nothing on it changed. Second, Google now stacks the top of the page with answer boxes (People Also Ask questions, image panels, and related-question blocks) that push the classic blue links down. On the RMBH keywords we checked, more than half carry a People Also Ask block and most carry an image or related-answer panel above the ordinary listings. Third, competitors publish and refresh pages too, and when a rival updates an article it can nudge one term for a while.

What this means for RMBH is simple: the foundation is healthy and category-leading. We are the loudest voice in our own space. The small position wobbles are normal weather, not a storm, and they are exactly what the maintenance side of the plan is built to catch. We watch the priority keywords every week, refresh the pages that drift, and answer the questions Google is now surfacing in those answer boxes, so RMBH keeps converting its presence into the clicks and donations that actually matter.
bullets: Share of organic traffic measures RMBH's slice of the combined search traffic across the tracked field. RMBH draws 48.25% of that traffic and ranks #1 of 4, 1.8x the next organization (Kupath Rabbi Meir at 26.72%). One keyword moving a spot does not dent that.

Giving demand is seasonal: Semrush shows searches for "donate to charity" swing about 4x and "jewish charity" over 6x between their quiet and peak months, so the same page naturally rises and falls with the calendar.

Google now places answer boxes (People Also Ask, image panels, related questions) above the regular links. More than half of the RMBH keywords we checked carry a People Also Ask block, pushing the classic listings down a notch.
Competitors refresh their pages too, so a rival update can nudge a single term temporarily without changing the overall standings.
This is normal weather. The maintenance plan watches priority keywords weekly, refreshes drifting pages, and targets the new answer boxes to keep our presence converting into clicks.
